fees: There are no additional fees or charges beyond the tuition costs listed above. All program materials, live classes, and support services are included in the tuition.
admissions: Basic computer literacy: navigate the internet, use standard software such as word processing and spreadsheets, and manage email communications.

English proficiency: speak, read, and write English well enough to engage with course materials, instructors, and peers. Non-native speakers may be required to provide evidence of proficiency, such as TOEFL or IELTS results, where applicable.
Minimum age: at least 18 years old at enrollment.
Education: a high school diploma or equivalent is recommended; no formal degree is required. Previous experience in technology, business, or project management is beneficial but not mandatory.
Technology: reliable access to a computer or laptop and a stable internet connection. Course materials, live sessions, and communications use online platforms.
tuitionReduction: Income brackets: documented income below specified thresholds, using Federal Poverty Level (FPL) guidelines.
Employment status: unemployment or underemployment verified by employment history or relevant documentation.
Geographic area: underserved or economically disadvantaged areas, based on publicly available regional economic data.
Hardship conditions: documented financial or personal hardships, including medical expenses or loss of employment.
refundIntroduction: At Mentor Agile, we offer a flexible refund policy to accommodate the needs of our students:

refundPolicy.title: Full Refund
refundPolicy.text: Students who cancel their enrollment before the first live session begins are eligible for a full refund of tuition fees paid.

refundPolicy.title: Partial Refund
refundPolicy.text: After the program commences, students may request a partial refund:
items: No refunds will be granted after two weeks of the program.

refundPolicy.title: Exceptional Circumstances
refundPolicy.text: In cases of unforeseen personal or medical emergencies, students may request a refund or deferment, which will be reviewed individually.

refundPolicy.title: Request Process
refundPolicy.text: Refund requests must be submitted in writing via email to admissions@mentoragile.com. Refunds will be processed within 14 business days of approval. The refund applies only to core tuition fees and excludes any optional materials or services already provided.

completion: Module quizzes: achieve 70% or higher on every end-of-module quiz. Students scoring below 70% may retake a quiz once, with additional instructor guidance before the retake.
Project-based assignments: successfully complete all hands-on assignments, graded pass/fail against the criteria provided. Collaboration and group discussions are encouraged.

Attendance and participation: attend at least 80% of live sessions and engage with course materials. Review missed sessions through recorded materials; notify the instructor in advance of an anticipated absence.

Final assessment: achieve at least 75% on the comprehensive final assessment, including a written component and a practical project. Complete the practical project to the standard specified by the instructors.

programs.name: Mentor Agile Product Owner/Product Manager (MAPOB)
programs.note: VIP is the rebranding of this same Product Owner/Product Manager program.
description: The Mentor Agile Product Owner/Product Manager (MAPOB) course is a 3-month immersive program designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge required to succeed in roles as Product Owners or Product Managers in Agile environments. The course covers Agile frameworks, including Scrum and Kanban, product management fundamentals, stakeholder engagement, and technical communication strategies. Students gain practical experience in backlog management, release planning, and team collaboration, preparing them for real-world challenges in tech-driven industries.
objectives: Master Agile methodologies, including Scrum and Kanban, and be able to facilitate core Agile ceremonies.
Manage product backlogs, including prioritization and refinement of user stories.
Define, manage, and validate Minimum Viable Products (MVPs).
Effectively engage and communicate with stakeholders across the product lifecycle.
Plan product releases and manage roadmaps to deliver value iteratively.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including development, design, and marketing.
Be prepared to apply for and succeed in Product Owner/Manager roles in the job market.

weeks.title: Weeks 1–3 · Beginner Phase
weeks.text: Agile principles, Scrum and Kanban frameworks, and core Agile ceremonies.

weeks.title: Weeks 4–6 · Intermediate Phase
weeks.text: Product backlog management, user stories, and MVP development.

weeks.title: Weeks 7–8 · Advanced Phase
weeks.text: Stakeholder engagement, release planning, and roadmap management.

weeks.title: Weeks 9–12 · Career Launchpad
weeks.text: Job preparation, resume building, interview techniques, and career strategy.

programs.tuitionIncludes: Includes 24 live classes over 12 weeks, recorded modules, resume development tools, interview preparation materials, and one-on-one career counseling.
certifications: Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO) — Scrum Alliance.
SAFe Product Owner/Product Manager (POPM) — Scaled Agile, Inc.
examProcess: After MAPOB course completion, Mentor Agile pays for and books the certification exam through an approved vendor listed by Scrum Alliance or Scaled Agile, Inc. Mentor Agile coordinates a date and time with the student.

Once booking is confirmed, the certification provider emails the student an access link for the scheduled certification session. Upon successful completion, the student can view their certification status and download a digital certificate from the provider’s portal.
Preparation includes mock tests, review sessions, and focused guidance on key certification topics.

programs.name: AI-Enhanced Pharmacy Technician & EKG Technician
programs.instruction: 160 clock hours · 10 live classes · Fully remote
programs.codes: CIP 51.0801 · SOC 29-2052 (Pharmacy Technicians). The catalog also lists SOC 29-2031 (Cardiovascular Technologists and Technicians).
description: An intensive 4-week, fully remote training program designed to prepare students for high-demand careers as Certified Pharmacy Technicians and EKG Technicians. Led by a residency-trained PharmD and practicing hospital pharmacist, this premium program blends AI-enhanced coursework with advanced virtual simulations, immersive VR skill labs, and interactive exercises covering pharmacy law, pharmacology, medication safety, prescription processing, calculations, and real-world pharmacy workflow training. To further elevate our student competitiveness, the program incorporates a comprehensive EKG Technician training track, including virtual lead placement, cardiac anatomy essentials, rhythm interpretation, and hands-on simulated patient scenarios. This dual-focus approach equips students with both pharmacy technician competencies and essential cardiovascular diagnostic skills widely valued across hospitals, clinics, and outpatient centers. Graduates emerge fully prepared to earn the Certified Pharmacy Technician (CPhT) and EKG Technician Certification, gaining practical skills, professional confidence, and job-ready expertise for retail, hospital, ambulatory, and clinical healthcare environments. Participants also receive personalized career coaching, resume development, interview preparation, and job-connection support, making this a truly premium, career-accelerating program designed to produce highly skilled candidates with exceptional value in today’s healthcare workforce.
objectives: Medications & Pharmacology Identify generic/brand names, classifications, and indications for common medications.
Interpret strengths, dosage forms, routes, and therapy durations, including stability and storage requirements.
Law & Professional Standards: Apply federal and state laws governing controlled and non-controlled substances, hazardous waste handling, recalls, DSCSA requirements, and pharmacy recordkeeping.
Patient Safety & Quality Assurance: Recognize high-alert and LASA medications, apply error-prevention strategies, and follow procedures for event reporting, CQI, and infection control.

Order Entry, Processing & Calculations: Perform all PTCE-level pharmacy calculations (dosage, days’ supply, concentrations, dilutions). Collect required patient/prescriber information, detect forged or invalid prescriptions,and prioritize workflow.
Nonsterile Compounding Compound basic nonsterile preparations (ointments, creams, suspensions, suppositories) using correct formulas, BUD assignment, documentation and environmental controls.
Inventory Management & Administrative Tasks Execute ordering, stock rotation, returns, reverse distribution, physical inventories, and support automated dispensing systems.
Health & Wellness Use monitoring devices (BP monitors, glucometers), recognize emergency symptoms, and assist with immunization and health-promotion documentation.
Billing & Reimbursement Process third-party claims, resolve rejections, understand Medicare/Medicaid and private plans, and support MTM and 340B-related workflows.

weeks.title: Week 1 · Foundations in Medications & Pharmacology
weeks.text: Core drug knowledge: brand/generic names, classifications, indications. Basic anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology linked to major organ systems. Understanding side effects, adverse effects, allergies, drug interactions, and contraindications.

weeks.title: Week 2 · Law, Standards & Professional Practice
weeks.text: HIPAA, OBRA-90, ADA, and requirements for consumer medication information and Med Guides.

weeks.title: Week 3 · Order Entry, Calculations, Compounding & Inventory
weeks.text: Pharmacy math & calculations: ratios, proportions, conversions, days’ supply, dosage calculations, IV and concentration math, and alligations. Order entry skills: collecting patient/prescriber data, prioritizing orders, verifying completeness, and spotting forged or altered prescriptions. Nonsterile compounding: preparing simple formulations, using proper documentation, assigning BUDs, and maintaining environmental controls.

weeks.title: Week 4 · Patient Safety, Health & Wellness, Billing & PTCE Bootcamp
weeks.text: Health & wellness: use of monitoring devices; emergency symptoms; risk factors for disease prevention and wellness services. PTCE preparation: full-length practice exam and prep.

programs.tuitionIncludes: Includes all program materials, 10 live classes, and support services.
certifications: Certified Pharmacy Technician (CPhT) — Pharmacy Technician Certification Board (PTCB).
Certified EKG Technician (CET) — National Healthcareer Association (NHA) / National Center for Competency Testing (NCCT), as listed in the catalog.
examProcess: After course completion, Mentor Agile pays for and books the PTCB certification exam for the pharmacy technician credential. Mentor Agile coordinates the exam date and time with each student.

After booking, the certification provider sends access instructions. Upon successful completion, students can view their active PTCB certification and download a digital copy from the provider’s portal.
Preparation includes mock tests, review sessions, and focused guidance. The catalog’s payment and booking commitment applies to the PTCB pharmacy technician exam.

programs.name: Retail Software QA Specialist
programs.codes: CIP 11.0899 (Computer Software and Media Applications) and CIP 52.1803 · SOC 15-1253 (Software QA Analysts and Testers)
description: The Retail Software QA Specialist program prepares students to perform User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and software quality assurance within a live retail environment. Students gain hands-on experience testing proprietary point-of-sale (POS) systems, store management platforms, and AI-powered retail technologies during real customer transactions. The program integrates Agile and Scrum methodologies with practical QA techniques, enabling students to evaluate software performance, identify defects, and provide actionable feedback to development teams. Emphasis is placed on ensuring that technology solutions function effectively in real-world retail settings while enhancing the overall customer experience.
objectives: Execute User Acceptance Testing (UAT) on POS systems and retail software in a live environment.
Identify, document, and report software defects using industry-standard tracking tools.
Apply Agile and Scrum principles to participate in software development and testing cycles.
Evaluate software functionality and performance during real customer interactions.
Test and validate AI-powered retail features such as product recommendations and customer-facing tools.

weeks.title: Week 1 · Scrum Foundations & QA Methodology (40 hours)
weeks.text: This week introduces students to Agile and Scrum principles, focusing on team structure, workflows, and the role of Quality Assurance within iterative development. Students will learn core QA methodologies, including defect tracking, test reporting, and Agile testing practices, while gaining foundational knowledge of POS systems. By the end of the week, students will be prepared to operate within a Scrum team and understand structured QA processes.

weeks.title: Week 2 · Retail Domain Expertise & Customer Service (40 hours)
weeks.text: Students will develop a strong understanding of the retail environment and customer behavior, learning how customer interactions influence technology and testing priorities. The week emphasizes customer service strategies, communication skills, and translating real-world customer pain points into actionable QA test cases. By the end of the week, students will be able to connect business needs with technical testing requirements.
details: Credential preparation: NRF RISE Up Customer Service & Sales.

weeks.title: Week 3 · AI Testing & Live Production Practicum (40 hours)
weeks.text: This week focuses on applying QA skills in real-world scenarios, including testing AI-powered retail systems and participating in live production environments. Students will design and execute User Acceptance Tests (UAT), document defects, and monitor system performance during active retail operations. By the end of the week, students will have hands-on experience testing live systems and producing professional QA reports.

weeks.title: Week 4 · Certification & Capstone (40 hours)
weeks.text: Students will consolidate their knowledge through certification preparation and a comprehensive capstone project. The focus is on demonstrating mastery of Scrum, QA practices, and retail technology through a detailed evaluation of an AI feature deployment. By the end of the week, students will be prepared for certification exams and equipped with practical experience to enter the workforce.
details: CSM and NRF RISE Up Customer Service & Sales exam preparation and completion.
Capstone: comprehensive QA evaluation report on an AI feature deployment and customer impact analysis using retail domain insights.
Career development: resume preparation, interview coaching, and job placement support.

programs.tuitionIncludes: Includes all program materials, live classes, and support services.
certifications: NRF RISE Up Customer Service & Sales — NRF Foundation.
examProcess: For CSM, students must complete the required instructional hours and actively participate in training before becoming eligible to sit for the certification exam. For NRF RISE Up Customer Service & Sales, students must complete the curriculum and pass the corresponding assessment.

Mentor Agile provides guided instruction, practice assessments, targeted review sessions, exam registration guidance, and scheduling assistance. Each certifying body maintains its own standards, exam structure, and passing requirements.

Mentor Agile does not administer these certification exams directly and cannot guarantee a passing outcome. Certification is awarded solely by the respective certifying organizations upon successful completion of their exam requirements.
